Likelihood-ratio test of nested models with the same number of classes

lrtest.Rd

The naive (ML) likelihood-ratio test of two nested models with the same number of classes, e.g. full against partial measurement invariance.

Usage

lrtest(restricted, full)

Arguments

restricted, full

Fitted latentmix models; full has more free parameters and restricted is nested in it.

Value

A one-row data frame with chisq, df, p and delta_bic (BIC of full minus BIC of restricted).

Details

The statistic is \(2(LL_{full} - LL_{restricted})\) on the difference in free parameters. It assumes ML, not MLR: with robust standard errors (the default in Mplus for mixtures) prefer the scaled test of compare_models(), which also reports this naive test.

See also

compare_models()

Examples

data(aces)
# \donttest{
# Is the ACE measurement model the same for women and men? (female: 0/1)
full <- lca(aces, starts_with("ace_"), K = 4, group = female)            # invariant items
#> Starting Julia ...
part <- lca(aces, starts_with("ace_"), K = 4, group = female,
            invariance = "ace_sex_abuse")                                 # one item free
lrtest(full, part)   # small p: sexual abuse is reported differently by sex (as generated)
#>      chisq df            p delta_bic
#> 1 43.61526  4 7.711627e-09 -14.36238
# under MLR use the scaled test: compare_models(full, part)
# }
